population: 24 people with metastatic melanoma and one with metastatic renal cancer.
finding: 3 of 18 sampled patients had viable bacteria recovered from a tumour. 25 were treated.
tissue_evidence: Table 3 lists tumour aspirate or excision cultures for 18 distinct patients. Three had at least one positive specimen. Seven of the 25 treated have no tumour-culture result listed.
safety: Dose-limiting effects at the highest dose included persistent bloodstream infection, low platelets, anaemia and gastrointestinal symptoms.
interpretation: In one patient, an aspirate was negative while an excision from the same lesion on the same day grew the bacteria. No objective tumour regressions were observed, including in the three culture-positive patients.
source_location: Table 3 and Results, tumour colonisation and toxicity

population: Four additional people with metastatic melanoma in a follow-up report.
finding: 1 of 4 sampled patients had a positive culture. One colony was recovered on day 5.
tissue_evidence: All four patients had excised tumour tissue tested. A single colony grew from the day-5 specimen. No growth was seen in the other three patients, whose tissue was taken on day 14.
safety: One patient developed grade 3 transient hypoxia and another had grade 3 low phosphate. The report gives no formal dose-limiting toxicity count.
interpretation: The day-5 and day-14 samples came from different people. These observations establish a single positive culture, without showing how long the bacteria persisted in that tumour.
source_location: Table 1, timing footnote and safety narrative

population: 25 people with advanced bone or soft-tissue sarcoma. Thirteen received IV treatment, eight intra-arterial treatment and four both.
finding: Tumour bacterial DNA was detected. The positive and tested patient counts are unreported.
tissue_evidence: The ASCO abstract reports a positive bacterial DNA signal by quantitative PCR. It gives no tested count, positive count, sampling time or delivery route for the positive specimens.
safety: The abstract gives no dose-limiting toxicity count. Fever was the most frequent treatment-related event (32%). No treatment-related deaths were reported.
interpretation: A DNA signal can establish the presence of bacterial material. The abstract does not establish viability or give a separate tissue result for the 13 IV-only patients.

population: Three people with refractory cancer in a pilot study.
finding: 2 of 3 sampled patients had viable bacteria in the injected tumour through at least day 15.
tissue_evidence: All three injected tumours were sampled. Cultures showed viable bacteria in two patients, with detection through at least day 15 in both.
safety: One patient withdrew after grade 3 chest pain of uncertain cause. The trial closed for nonmedical reasons before a maximum tolerated dose was established.
interpretation: This establishes persistence at the injection site in two people. Travel from the bloodstream to a distant tumour is a separate question.

population: 24 people with treatment-refractory advanced solid tumours.
finding: 10 of 24 showed clinical or imaging signs of germination. One case has direct tissue confirmation. The cohort culture rate is unknown.
tissue_evidence: Investigators assessed local germination using clinical and imaging findings. Eight patients gave paired biopsies to assess immune infiltration. The culture-positive fraction for the whole cohort is unreported.
safety: Three dose-limiting events were reported. Two patients developed grade 4 sepsis and one developed grade 4 gas gangrene.
interpretation: A separate report of the first participant describes a positive tumour aspirate culture and bacteria visible on biopsy. It is one case from this same cohort.
source_location: Results, germination, safety and host immune response

population: 32 people with refractory advanced cancers, 24 on monotherapy and eight with atezolizumab.
finding: Bacterial DNA was undetectable in day-7 tumour samples after direct injection. The tested patient count is unstated.
tissue_evidence: The report describes a negative strain-specific DNA assay in day-7 tumour aspirates. It does not state how many patients contributed to that assay result.
safety: Five cytokine release syndrome events occurred on monotherapy. One grade 3 event met the trial’s dose-limiting toxicity criteria.
interpretation: The 12 patients with paired core biopsies contributed to a later immune gene-expression analysis. Using 12 or 32 as the day-7 bacterial test denominator would answer the wrong question.

population: Preoperative colorectal study with 35 recruited. The human paired-tissue analysis included six probiotic recipients and two placebo recipients.
finding: Six active and two placebo recipients had evaluable paired tissue. Tumour enrichment varied between participants.
tissue_evidence: The team compared paired neoplastic and normal bowel tissue using culture followed by strain-specific PCR. Two of six probiotic recipients did not show preferential tumour enrichment.
safety: This preoperative study investigated colonisation with a probiotic. A dose-limiting toxicity count was not reported.
interpretation: The comparison measures relative signal in paired tissues. An absolute patient-level culture-positive rate cannot be read from that result. The human arm studied the unmodified probiotic.
source_location: Figure 2J–K, human study Methods and Discussion
